- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak for 3–7 days.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is rising, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast for next 5–10 days.
- Model underperforms when sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is trending; use 3-day moving average of history to anchor forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% for 3+ consecutive days, adjust downward by 1–2% per day until trend stabilizes.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for remaining days.
- Model often misses mean reversion in 10–15 day windows; if price deviates >3σ from 30-day mean, apply mean-reversion correction at 1–2% per day.
